exposure: Peak systolic velocities in the pulmonary artery trunk (PSV-PA) at diagnosis of PS
Interval between diagnosis of TTTS and diagnosis of PS
outcome: In utero regression of PS after laser treatment
Need for cardiac intervention (valvular dilatation) after birth
cohort: The study included 2091 monochorionic diamniotic (MCDA) pregnancies, focusing on the 24 cases diagnosed with isolated pulmonary stenosis, particularly those complicated by twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS).
finding: An elevated peak systolic velocities in the pulmonary artery trunk (PSV-PA) at the time of PS diagnosis and a short time-interval between fetoscopic laser surgery and PS diagnosis are predictive of the need for interventional treatment after birth.
